# Clustering at TSS within Pol II ChIP peaks

The goal of the this analysis is to see promoter states at TSS. The reads that enter the clustering must have a Pol II ChIP-seq peak and have a 30-60 bp long footprint within the read

A read is eligible if it covers the whole 2 kb window around a selected TSS and carries a 30–60 bp FiberHMM footprint in that window. Clustering then uses a random 5,000 of the eligible molecules

**To calculate the m6a proportions in each clusters, each of 40 bins of 50 bp**, I used possible m6a positions pooled from all eligible reads at that TSS, including reads without a footprint

1. denominator: observed A/T sites. For each TSS, every full-span read there is pooled, across all 31 samples and including reads without a footprint. Any position, relative to the TSS, where at least one of those reads has an m6A call counts as an observed site

2. for each read r at TSS t and each of the 40 bins of 50 bp

  - methylation(r, bin) = (r's m6a calls in the bin) / (observed sites at t in that bin)

3. cluster methylation profile

  - profile(cluster, bin) = mean over methylation(r, bin)

**Dominant TSS for each gene are used, which is selected as:**

1. Build the consensus of CAGE TSS

- Each input record represents a single genomic base with a CAGE tag count and strand. A site is retained only if the exact same base on the same strand has at least one tag in all three replicates. Nearby bases are not merged into clusters

2. Sum tag counts across the 3 replicates

3. Find nearby annotated GENCODE v46 TSS near the consensus site in 3 replicates

  - Use GENCODE v46 transcripts on chromosomes 1–22 and X. A consensus site is eligible for a transcript if it is on the same chromosome and strand and lies within 250 bp of its annotated TSS, in either direction. All transcript isoforms are considered

4. Exclude CAGE TSS beyond the transcript end

5. Assign each consensus site to one gene

  - Among eligible transcript matches, retain those with the smallest distance to an annotated TSS. If equally close matches belong to different genes, discard that CAGE site as ambiguous. Multiple equally close transcript matches within one gene can remain
  
6. Choose the dominant CAGE consensus TSS for each gene

  - Select the assigned site with the highest summed CAGE count
  
  
**I also want to connect pausing index to the clustes, so I calculated pausing index following the steps by Day et al. 2016 using Pol II ChIP-seq data**

1. Start with hg38 RefSeq transcripts on chromosomes 1–22 and X. Remove genes whose isoforms occur on multiple chromosomes or strands

2. Pool seven Pol II ChIP-seq replicates and, separately, two input-control replicates. Within each replicate, collapse reads sharing the same genomic 5′ position and strand. Each remaining read contributes one count at its 5′ end. Region counts combine both read strands

3. Measure signal around each candidate TSS (TSSR)

  - For every distinct annotated TSS, define a 350-bp TSS region: −50 through +299 bp, oriented in the direction of transcription
  
  - Normalize ChIP and input counts separately: 
 
 $$\text{density} = \frac{\text{region read count}}{\text{region length in bp} \times \left(\frac{\text{pooled library reads}}{10^6}\right)}$$
  
  - Then subtract background: corrected signal="ChIP density − input density
  
4. Choose one TSS and transcript per gene

  - Select the annotated TSS with the highest corrected TSS-region signal. If multiple transcripts share that TSS, choose the longest transcript, which determines the transcript end

5. Measure gene-body signal. Define the body as +300 bp after the selected TSS through 3,000 bp beyond the transcript end, following transcription direction. Calculate its length-normalized, library-normalized ChIP density and subtract the corresponding input density, as above

6. Calculate the pausing index

  - $PI = \frac{\text{corrected TSS-region signal}}{\text{corrected gene-body signal}}$
  
Calculate PI only when the corrected TSS-region signal is ≥0.001 reads per million per bp and corrected body signal is >0. Otherwise, record PI as missing. For example, TSS-region signal of 0.02 and body signal of 0.005 give PI = 4





## Clustering

clusters individual Fiber-seq molecules by their m6A accessibility patterns around TSSs, pooling all 31 LCL samples

	1. select TSSs associated with Pol II. Start with dominant FANTOM5 TSSs on chromosomes 1–22 and X. Keep a TSS only if its exact position overlaps a reproducible Pol II ChIP-seq peak
	
	2. define a 2-kb window around each TSS. Use positions −1,000 through +999, oriented by the gene’s strand so that upstream and downstream align consistently. Exclude windows extending beyond chromosome boundaries
	
	3. select eligible molecules. A molecule must span the entire 2-kb window and have at least one FiberHMM footprint of 30–60 bp overlapping that window, using footprint calls from its own sample. This footprint criterion does not itself establish that the footprint is Pol II
	
	4. build the m6A accessibility profile. Divide each window into 40 bins of 50 bp. For each bin: Identify distinct genomic positions with an m6A call in any full-window molecule pooled across samples, including molecules without qualifying footprints
	
	- divide each eligible molecule’s distinct m6A calls in the bin by that number of observed positions
	
	- For example, in one 50-bp bin:
	
	Across all full-span molecules, 20 distinct genomic positions have an m6A call somewhere
	
	- read A has modifications at 6 of those positions -> 6/20 = 0.30
	- read B has modifications at 10 of those positions -> 10/20 = 0.50
	
	5. sample molecules for clustering. Randomly select 5,000 distinct molecules from the pooled eligible population, without replacement. If a selected molecule qualifies at multiple TSSs, randomly choose one of its eligible TSS observations. Sampling is global, without equal quotas per sample or TSS
	
	6. measure similarity between molecules. Compare their 40-bin profiles using Manhattan distance
	
	7. identify clusters. Connect each molecule to its 10 nearest neighbors, giving stronger weights to more similar molecules. Run Leiden clustering with resolution 1 to identify groups with similar profiles
	
	8. assign the remaining molecules to the discovered clusters
	
		a. only the sampled 5000 molecules are used to discovered the clusters, the remaining eligible molecules are assigned to the existing clusters
		b. take one remaining molecule's binned accessibility profile --> find 10 sampled molecules with the most similar profiles by Manhattan distance
		c. count their cluster labels, assign the remaining molecules to the cluster with the most counts

- If there is a tie, compare the closest neighboring belong the 2 clusters, whichever of those clusters has the closet neighbor (by smallest distance) wins

Pol II fold-enrichment is measured over each candidate footprint. The boxplot
summarizes a molecule's footprints first, to avoid giving molecules with several
footprints extra weight. Bulk Pol II signal is shared locus evidence, not an independent
measurement of polymerase binding on each molecule.

```{r signal, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
signal <- fp[, .(signal = if (all(is.na(pol2_mean))) NA_real_ else mean(pol2_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(cluster, observation_id)]
ggplot(signal, aes(cluster, signal)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Mean Pol II fold-enrichment across candidate footprints")
```

PI is joined by Ensembl gene ID; the RefSeq TSS of `pause_index.tsv` can differ from the
FANTOM5 TSS used here.

```{r pi, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
pi_sites <- unique(m[, .(cluster, tss_id, pi)])

          scale_y_log10() + theme_bw() + labs(y = "PI (one value per TSS within each cluster)"))
} else cat("No matching PI values have been supplied.")
```

## Example loci

All eligible molecules at the FANTOM5 TSS of each gene in `locus_genes` (config), drawn
with `plot_locus_molecules()` from `parsing_functions/plotting_functions.r`. It is the
HSCA domain/CTCF figure without its CTCF, loop and domain tracks. Clustered molecules
keep their Leiden cluster. Every other molecule at the TSS takes the majority cluster of
its 10 nearest clustered molecules (Manhattan distance on the 40 bin features). The bars
compare the cluster proportions at the TSS with those of all clustered molecules.
Diamonds mark the gene's GTEx v8 LCL eVariants in the window.

```{r loci, include=FALSE}
loci <- pol2_observed_loci(cfg, x, annotation, observed_masks)
```


## Selected promoters: motif and read-level cluster examples

One promoter per cluster: among protein-coding TSSs with at least 100 eligible reads
present in all 31 samples, the TSS with the highest fraction of its reads in that
cluster. Reads are all eligible reads at the TSS: clustered reads keep their labels,
the others use the saved nearest-neighbour projections.

```{r promoter-motif-selection}
selected_promoters <- pol2_select_example_promoters(cfg)
knitr::kable(selected_promoters[, .(cluster, gene_name, n_cluster, n_total, n_samples, fraction)], digits = 3)
```

The selected promoters are `r paste(selected_promoters$gene_name, collapse = ", ")`.
Accessibility profiles use pooled observed m6A-call sites with no smoothing.
Each figure contains one promoter window and all eight motif families, using all eligible
reads at that promoter. Original reads retain their clustering labels; additional
reads use the saved nearest-neighbour cluster projections. These are descriptive
examples selected for cluster concentration, not tests of motif enrichment.

For each family, only the hit with the highest FIMO score in this window is shown
(ties: smaller p-value, matrix ID, position, strand). All motif segments are black.
Yellow shading marks every displayed motif interval. The shading is a reference
sequence annotation shared by the promoter's reads, not a footprint-support call.
TF blocks retain the standard 10–30, 30–60 and 60–80-bp colors; 130–160-bp nucleosome
blocks are retained. No TF score or FIRE-containment filter is applied. Support
counts use one individual 10–30-bp block covering at least 50% of one full motif
interval on that same read. U1 is omitted as requested.

```{r promoter-motif-analysis, include=FALSE}
promoter_motif_examples <- local({
  tables <- file.path(cfg$output, "tables")
  tabdir <- file.path(tables, "promoter_motif_cluster_examples")
  shared_read_cache <- file.path(tabdir,"promoter_read_data.rds")
  if (!is.null(example_gene)) tabdir <- file.path(tabdir,example_gene)
  plotdir <- file.path(cfg$output, "plots", "promoter_motif_cluster_examples")
  dir.create(tabdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(plotdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  selected <- copy(selected_promoters)
  if (!is.null(example_gene)) {
    selected <- selected[gene_name==example_gene]
    if (nrow(selected)!=1L) stop("--gene must be one of the seven selected example promoters")
  }
  prep <- readRDS(file.path(tables, "prepared.rds"))
  promoters <- prep$tss[match(selected$tss_id, tss_id)]
  stopifnot(identical(promoters$tss_id, selected$tss_id))
  families <- c("TATA","YY1","NFY","SP","ETS","ZNF143","NRF1","CREB")
  # Scan and BED extraction run in the motif-inputs preparation job.
  motif_path <- file.path(tables,"promoter_motif_cluster_examples","matrix_motif_hits.tsv.gz")
  if (!is.null(example_gene) && file.exists(file.path(tabdir,"matrix_motif_hits.tsv.gz")))
    motif_path <- file.path(tabdir,"matrix_motif_hits.tsv.gz")
  if (!file.exists(motif_path)) stop("Run --stage motif-inputs before knitting")
  hits <- fread(motif_path)[tss_id %in% selected$tss_id]
  stopifnot(all(hits$tss_id %in% selected$tss_id), all(hits$category %in% families))
  hits[, `:=`(width = end-start, xmin = relative_start-.5, xmax = relative_end+.5)]
  fwrite(selected, file.path(tabdir, "selected_promoters.tsv"), sep = "\t")
  fwrite(data.table(category = families, status = "available"),
         file.path(tabdir,"motif_category_status.tsv"),sep="\t")
  # Saved local data avoids repeatedly querying 31 sample files on report renders.
  cache_path <- file.path(tabdir,"promoter_read_data.rds")
  input_paths <- c(file.path(tables,c("prepared.rds","clustering.rds","tracks/molecule_projection.tsv.gz")),
    file.path(tables,"features",paste0(unique(promoters$chrom),".rds")))
  cache_key <- list(tss_id=selected$tss_id, inputs=pol2_stamp(input_paths))
  if (!is.null(example_gene) && !file.exists(cache_path) && file.exists(shared_read_cache)) {
    shared <- readRDS(shared_read_cache)
    stopifnot(all(selected$tss_id %in% names(shared$data)),
      identical(shared$key$inputs,pol2_stamp(shared$key$inputs$path)))
    saveRDS(list(key=cache_key,data=shared$data[selected$tss_id]),cache_path)
  }
  if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
    cached <- readRDS(cache_path)
    stopifnot(identical(cached$key,cache_key))
    local_data <- cached$data
  } else {
    stop("Missing promoter read cache: run --stage motif-inputs before knitting")
  }
  displayed_motifs <- list(); figures <- list(); overview <- list(); highlight_rows <- list(); read_rows <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(promoters))) {
    site <- promoters[i]; gene <- site$gene_name; tid <- site$tss_id
    dat <- local_data[[tid]]; rows <- copy(dat$meta)
    rows[, cluster := factor(cluster,levels=pol2_numeric_clusters(cluster))]
    setorder(rows,cluster,m6a_proportion,observation_id)
    rows[, RID := observation_id]
    rows <- as.data.table(stack_rows(as.data.frame(rows),"cluster"))
    stopifnot(nrow(rows)==selected$n_total[i],!anyDuplicated(rows$RID))
    cols <- cluster_id_palette(levels(rows$cluster))
    labels <- rows[,.(n=.N),by=cluster]
    labels <- setNames(sprintf("%s (n=%d)",labels$cluster,labels$n),labels$cluster)
    rr <- list(assignments=as.data.frame(rows),region=list(analysis_start=-1000L,analysis_end=999L))
    profile <- pol2_observed_profile(dat$calls,rows,observed_masks,rep(tid,nrow(rows)))
    fwrite(profile,file.path(tabdir,paste0(gene,"_observed_site_profile.tsv.gz")),sep="\t")
    profile <- profile[n_observed_reads>0]
    tracks <- dat$blocks[,.(RID=observation_id,start=rel_start,end=rel_end,class)]
    tracks[, class := factor(class,levels=names(MOLECULE_TRACK_COLORS))]
    setorder(tracks,class)
    ex <- data.frame(chrom=site$chrom,start=0,end=0,window_start=-1000,window_end=1000)
    lim <- molecule_xlim(ex,1L)
    read_rows[[gene]] <- rows[,.(gene,observation_id,tss_id,sample_name,original_RID,cluster,clustered)]
    hh <- copy(hits[tss_id==tid])
    setorderv(hh,c("category","score","p_value","matrix_id","relative_start","motif_strand"),
      c(1L,-1L,1L,1L,1L,1L))
    hh <- hh[, .SD[1L], by=category]
    displayed_motifs[[gene]] <- copy(hh)
    band <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(hh)), function(j)
      list(xmin=hh$xmin[j],xmax=hh$xmax[j],fill="yellow",alpha=.3,position="under"))
    highlight_rows[[gene]] <- hh[,.(gene,category,matrix_id,matrix_hit_id,tss_id,xmin,xmax,width)]
      top <- plot_group_profile(profile,group_col="cluster",x_col="pos",y_col="met",style="area",smooth_k=1L,
        facet_col="cluster",facet_layout="grid",colors=cols,fill_colors=cols,highlight=band,
        labels=list(x=NULL,y="m6A fraction (observed sites)"),theme=theme_fiberseq("classic",base_size=9)) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim=lim,expand=FALSE) + theme(legend.position="none")
      hh[, label := factor(category,levels=rev(families))]
      motif_labels <- setNames(paste(families,"(no hit)"),families)
      motif_labels[hh$category] <- paste(hh$category,hh$matrix_id)
      motif <- plot_interval_track(hh,lim,start_col="xmin",end_col="xmax",row_col="label",
        geometry="segment",color="black",linewidth=1.1,highlight=band,
        scales=list(y=scale_y_discrete(limits=rev(families),labels=motif_labels,drop=FALSE,expand=expansion(add=.55)),
          coord=coord_cartesian(xlim=lim,expand=FALSE)),labels=list(x=NULL,y="Motif"),
        theme=theme_fiberseq("classic",base_size=8))
      molecules <- plot_molecules(as.data.frame(rows),as.data.frame(tracks),ex,"cluster",labels,
        bar_cols="cluster",bar_palette=cols,track_colors=MOLECULE_TRACK_COLORS,breaks=seq(-1000,1000,250)) +
        labs(x="Position relative to this promoter's TSS (bp); oriented by transcription")
      molecules <- .fiberseq_add_highlights(molecules,band)
      # Support refers to the displayed highest-score hit, using full genomic intervals.
      eligible <- dat$blocks[kind=="tf" & length>=10 & length<=30]
      for (family in families) {
        hit <- hh[category==family]
        ov <- findOverlaps(pol2_gr(rep(site$chrom,nrow(hit)),hit$start,hit$end),
                           pol2_gr(eligible$chrom,eligible$start,eligible$end),ignore.strand=TRUE)
        q <- queryHits(ov); u <- subjectHits(ov)
        frac <- (pmin(hit$end[q],eligible$end[u])-pmax(hit$start[q],eligible$start[u]))/hit$width[q]
        supported <- unique(eligible$observation_id[u[frac>=.5]])
        counts <- rows[,.(n_reads=.N,n_supported=sum(observation_id %in% supported)),by=cluster]
        counts[, `:=`(gene=gene,tss_id=tid,category=family,n_hits=nrow(hit),
          n_scan_hits=nrow(hits[tss_id==tid & category==family]))]
        overview[[paste(gene,family)]] <- counts
      }
      heights <- c(.65*uniqueN(rows$cluster),1.8,.025*nrow(rows)+.15*uniqueN(rows$cluster)+.7)
      name <- paste(gene,"promoter_motif_cluster_examples",sep="_")
      fig <- patchwork::wrap_plots(top,motif,molecules,ncol=1,heights=heights) +
        patchwork::plot_annotation(title=paste(gene,"promoter motifs and cluster reads"),
          subtitle=sprintf("%s:%s (%s), hg38; %d eligible reads, %d samples; target %s.\nBlack: highest FIMO score per family. Yellow: each displayed motif. Standard footprint colors.",
            site$chrom,site$tss,site$strand,nrow(rows),uniqueN(rows$sample_name),selected$cluster[i]),
          theme=theme(plot.title=element_text(size=11),plot.subtitle=element_text(size=8)))
      save_figure(fig,file.path(plotdir,paste0(name,".pdf")),width=12,height=1.5+sum(heights))
      figures[[name]] <- list(plot=fig,height=1.5+sum(heights),gene=gene)
    message("Saved promoter motif figures: ",gene)
  }
  fwrite(rbindlist(displayed_motifs),file.path(tabdir,"displayed_motifs.tsv"),sep="\t")
  fwrite(rbindlist(overview),file.path(tabdir,"promoter_cluster_motif_support.tsv"),sep="\t")
  fwrite(rbindlist(highlight_rows),file.path(tabdir,"highlighted_motifs.tsv"),sep="\t")
  fwrite(rbindlist(read_rows),file.path(tabdir,"displayed_reads.tsv.gz"),sep="\t")
  list(figures=figures,selected=selected,summary=rbindlist(overview))
})
```

## Imprinted loci

Counts use all projected eligible physical molecules, deduplicated by RID within
cluster. Molecules seen at both imprinted and other TSSs appear only in the
imprinted composition bar. These comparisons are descriptive; no test is applied.

```{r imprinting, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.5}
imprinting <- pol2_imprinting(cfg,
  fread(file.path(params$output,"tables","tracks","molecule_projection.tsv.gz")),
  readRDS(file.path(params$output,"tables/prepared.rds"))$tss, clusters)
pol2_plot_imprinting(imprinting, clusters)
knitr::kable(imprinting$loci, digits = 3)
```

## Features of the 5,000 clustered molecules

m6A uses the stored calls and observed-site denominators from all full-span reads
at each TSS; its pooled fraction is sum(calls) / sum(positions). CpG uses
pb-CpG-tools count mode on these molecules, restricted to their cluster's TSS
windows. CpG boxplots assign each molecule its cluster/TSS fraction; the pooled
fraction counts each genomic CpG once per cluster. GRO-cap is the sense-strand
read sum over the full 2 kb window; DNase is the mean over that window.
Diamonds show pooled methylation fractions or molecule-weighted mean signal.
GRO-cap and DNase are plotted as log10(x + 1). Saved result tables permit
re-plotting without extracting CpG again.

```{r cluster-features, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
features <- list(
  molecules = fread(file.path(params$output, "tables", "cluster_features", "cluster_feature_molecules.tsv.gz")),
  summary = fread(file.path(params$output, "tables", "cluster_features", "cluster_features.tsv")))
pol2_plot_cluster_features(features, clusters)
knitr::kable(features$summary, digits = 3)
```

## autocorrelation profile per read for each cluster


Computed by `--stage autocorrelation`

```{r autocorrelation-analysis, include=FALSE}
local({
# Shared R functions compute ACFs, peaks and cluster summaries.
# Source with cfg and optionally acf_action="plot" to load plots without computing.
tables <- file.path(cfg$output, "tables")
acf_tables <- file.path(tables,"autocorrelation")
dir.create(acf_tables,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
if (!file.exists(file.path(acf_tables,"autocorrelation_cluster_summary.tsv.gz")) &&
    !isTRUE(get0("recompute_autocorrelation",ifnotfound=FALSE))) stop("Run --stage autocorrelation before knitting")
acf_action <- if (isTRUE(get0("recompute_autocorrelation",ifnotfound=FALSE)) || !file.exists(file.path(acf_tables,"autocorrelation_cluster_summary.tsv.gz"))) "compute" else "plot"
if (acf_action == "compute") {
  x <- readRDS(file.path(tables,"clustering.rds"))
  m <- data.table::fread(file.path(tables,"molecule_assignments.tsv.gz"))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(m$observation_id),nrow(m)==nrow(x$molecules))
  index <- match(m$observation_id,x$molecules$observation_id)
  for (field in c("sample_name","original_RID","tss_id","cluster"))
    stopifnot(identical(as.character(m[[field]]),as.character(x$molecules[[field]][index])))
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(x$sites),as.character(-1000:999)))
  sites <- as.matrix(x$sites[match(m$observation_id,rownames(x$sites)),,drop=FALSE])
  if (!exists("pol2_observed_masks")) source(file.path(cfg$project,"code/pausing/clustering_Pol2/pol2_chip_cluster_utils/pol2_observed_profiles.R"))
  masks <- pol2_observed_masks(cfg,x)[m$tss_id,,drop=FALSE]
  m[, upstream_observed_sites := rowSums(masks[,as.character(-500:-25),drop=FALSE])]
  m[, downstream_observed_sites := rowSums(masks[,as.character(25:500),drop=FALSE])]
  shared <- file.path(cfg$project, "code/clustering_methods/auto_correlation")
  source(file.path(shared, "02_compute_autocorrelations.R"), local = TRUE)
  source(file.path(shared, "04_summarize_autocorrelations.R"), local = TRUE)
  windows <- list(upstream = c(-500L, -25L), downstream = c(25L, 500L))
  curves <- stats <- molecule_tables <- list()
  for (window_name in names(windows)) {
    bounds <- windows[[window_name]]
    result <- autocorrelations(sites, positions = -1000:999, window = bounds)
    profiles <- result$profiles
    selected <- sites[, as.character(seq.int(bounds[1L], bounds[2L])), drop = FALSE]
    records <- as.data.frame(m)
    records$cluster <- as.integer(sub("cluster", "", records$cluster, fixed = TRUE))
    stopifnot(!anyNA(records$cluster))
    records$status <- ifelse(result$valid, "clustered", "zero_variance")
    records$region_id <- window_name
    records$n_observed_sites <- records[[paste0(window_name, "_observed_sites")]]
    records$m6a_call_fraction <- rowSums(selected) / ifelse(
      records$n_observed_sites > 0, records$n_observed_sites, NA_real_)
    summary <- summarize_autocorrelations(profiles, records)
    annotate <- function(table) {
      table$cluster <- if (nrow(table)) paste0("cluster", table$cluster) else character()
      table$window <- rep(window_name, nrow(table))
      table$window_start_bp <- rep(bounds[1L], nrow(table))
      table$window_end_bp <- rep(bounds[2L], nrow(table))
      table
    }
    averages <- annotate(summary$averages)
    summaries <- annotate(summary$summaries)
    curves[[window_name]] <- averages[, c("cluster", "window", "window_start_bp",
      "window_end_bp", "lag_bp", "mean_acf")]
    stats[[window_name]] <- summaries[, c("cluster", "window", "window_start_bp",
      "window_end_bp", "positive_local_peak_140_250_bp", "peak_acf")]
    records <- annotate(records)
    records$cluster <- m$cluster
    peaks <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(profiles)), function(i) repeat_peak(profiles[i, ]), numeric(2L)))
    records$positive_local_peak_140_250_bp <- peaks[, 1L]
    records$peak_acf <- peaks[, 2L]
    molecule_tables[[window_name]] <- records
    saveRDS(list(acf = profiles, lag_bp = seq_len(ncol(selected)) - 1L,
      relative_bp = seq.int(bounds[1L], bounds[2L]), observation_id = m$observation_id,
      window = window_name), file.path(acf_tables,
        paste0("autocorrelation_per_molecule_", window_name, ".rds")))
  }
  data.table::fwrite(data.table::rbindlist(curves),
    file.path(acf_tables, "autocorrelation_cluster_summary.tsv.gz"), sep = "\t")
  data.table::fwrite(data.table::rbindlist(stats),
    file.path(acf_tables, "autocorrelation_cluster_peaks.tsv"), sep = "\t")
  data.table::fwrite(data.table::rbindlist(molecule_tables),
    file.path(acf_tables, "autocorrelation_molecules.tsv.gz"), sep = "\t")
  saveRDS(list(window=list(upstream=c(-500,-25),downstream=c(25,500)),lags=c(0,475),
    method="R autocorrelations(), summarize_autocorrelations(), repeat_peak(); binary 1-bp m6A",
    source_md5=tools::md5sum(file.path(shared, c("02_compute_autocorrelations.R", "04_summarize_autocorrelations.R"))),
    input_md5=tools::md5sum(file.path(tables,c("clustering.rds","molecule_assignments.tsv.gz")))),
    file.path(acf_tables,"autocorrelation_provenance.rds"))
}

audit_path <- file.path(acf_tables,"autocorrelation_molecules.tsv.gz")
audit <- fread(audit_path)
if (!"n_observed_sites" %in% names(audit)) {
  saved <- readRDS(file.path(tables,"clustering.rds"))
  if (!exists("pol2_observed_masks")) source(file.path(cfg$project,"code/pausing/clustering_Pol2/pol2_chip_cluster_utils/pol2_observed_profiles.R"))
  mask <- pol2_observed_masks(cfg,saved)
  for (window_name in c("upstream","downstream")) {
    ii <- which(audit$window==window_name)
    pos <- if (window_name=="upstream") -500:-25 else 25:500
    numerator <- as.numeric(Matrix::rowSums(saved$sites[audit$observation_id[ii],as.character(pos),drop=FALSE]))
    denominator <- rowSums(mask[audit$tss_id[ii],as.character(pos),drop=FALSE])
    audit[ii, `:=`(n_observed_sites=denominator,
      m6a_call_fraction=ifelse(denominator>0,numerator/denominator,NA_real_))]
  }
  fwrite(audit,audit_path,sep="\t")
}
})
```

## Nucleosome positioning at TSS of each cluster



Computed by `--stage nucleosome`

```{r nucleosome-analysis, include=FALSE}
if (!file.exists(file.path(cfg$output,"tables","nuc","nucleosome_cluster_summary.tsv.gz")) &&
    !isTRUE(get0("recompute_nucleosome",ifnotfound=FALSE))) stop("Run --stage nucleosome before knitting")
if (isTRUE(get0("recompute_nucleosome",ifnotfound=FALSE)) ||
    !file.exists(file.path(cfg$output,"tables","nuc","nucleosome_cluster_summary.tsv.gz"))) local({

      
source(file.path(cfg$project,"code/nucleosome_positioning/process_nuc_pos.R"),local=TRUE)
tables <- file.path(cfg$output,"tables")
nuc_tables <- file.path(tables,"nuc")
dir.create(nuc_tables,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
prep <- readRDS(file.path(tables,"prepared.rds"))
x <- readRDS(file.path(tables,"clustering.rds"))
m <- fread(file.path(tables,"molecule_assignments.tsv.gz"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(m$observation_id),nrow(m)==nrow(x$molecules))
idx <- match(m$observation_id,x$molecules$observation_id)
for (field in c("sample_name","original_RID","tss_id","cluster","tss","strand"))
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(m[[field]]),as.character(x$molecules[[field]][idx])))
clusters <- pol2_numeric_clusters(m$cluster)
m[, cluster:=factor(cluster,levels=clusters)]
site <- prep$tss[match(unique(m$tss_id),tss_id)]
anchors <- build_region_anchors(NULL,NULL,NULL,relative_window=c(-1000L,999L),
  anchor_table=site[,.(region_id=tss_id,chr=chrom,anchor=tss,strand,region_type="promoter",gene=gene_name,ensg=gene_id)])
stopifnot(all(anchors$view_start==site$window_start+1L),all(anchors$view_end==site$window_end))
reads <- build_read_table(m[,.(region_id=tss_id,RID=observation_id,sample_name,original_RID,
  biological_sample=cell_line,cluster,read_start,read_end)],anchors)
reads[,`:=`(rel_read_start=pmax(rel_read_start,-1000L),rel_read_end=pmin(rel_read_end,999L))]
stopifnot(all(reads$rel_read_start == -1000L),all(reads$rel_read_end == 999L))
paths <- setNames(file.path(cfg$footprint_dir,prep$samples$sample_name,
  paste0(prep$samples$sample_name,".recalled_footprint.bed.gz")),prep$samples$sample_name)
footprints <- extract_region_footprints(reads,anchors,input_paths=paths,include_tf=FALSE,original_id_col="original_RID")
footprints <- merge(footprints,reads[,.(region_id,RID,sample_name,original_RID,biological_sample,cluster)],
  by=c("region_id","RID","sample_name"))
pos <- read_position_summary(footprints,reads,include_gap=FALSE)
strata <- position_summary_by_group(pos,by=c("region_id","cluster","sample_name"),include_gap=FALSE)
summary <- position_summary_by_group(pos,by="cluster",include_gap=FALSE,bootstrap=500L,sample_col="biological_sample")
occupancy <- occupancy_profile(footprints,reads,anchors,by=c("region_id","cluster","sample_name"))
centers <- occupancy_profile(footprints,reads,anchors,by=c("region_id","cluster","sample_name"),bin_size=25L,metric="centers")

occ_profile <- occupancy[,.(value=sum(n_occupied)/sum(n_reads),
  raw_count=sum(n_occupied),denominator=sum(n_reads)),by=.(cluster,pos)]
center_profile <- centers[,.(value=sum(n_centers),raw_count=sum(n_centers)),
  by=.(cluster,pos,bin_start,bin_end_exclusive,bin_width_bp)]
objects <- list(molecules=pos,footprints=footprints,occupancy_profiles=occ_profile,center_counts_profiles=center_profile,
  cluster_summary=summary,positional_strata=strata,occupancy_strata=occupancy,center_counts_strata=centers[,!"density"],
  centers=footprints[,.(region_id,RID,sample_name,original_RID,biological_sample,cluster,fp_start,fp_end,rel_mid)])
for (name in names(objects)) fwrite(objects[[name]],file.path(nuc_tables,paste0("nucleosome_",name,".tsv.gz")),sep="\t")
saveRDS(list(window=c(-1000L,999L),input_paths=paths,source="FiberHMM recalled_footprint BED13; all blocks; no size filter",
  selection="Existing Pol II footprint-positive accessibility clusters",position_method="Original midpoint-based -1/+1; no gap",
  uncertainty="TSS occupancy: 500 crossed promoter x biological-sample bootstrap draws; no molecule resampling",
  inputs=tools::md5sum(file.path(tables,c("clustering.rds","prepared.rds","molecule_assignments.tsv.gz")))),
  file.path(nuc_tables,"nucleosome_provenance.rds"))
})
```

## Expression and pausing index

Expression is mean ENCSR820PHH gene TPM across the two configured replicates,
joined by version-stripped Ensembl gene ID. Each TSS is represented once per
cluster; the summaries are descriptive and TSSs shared between clusters are not
independent biological replicates.

```{r expression-analysis, include=FALSE}
expression_result <- local({
tables <- file.path(cfg$output, "tables")

expr <- rbindlist(lapply(cfg$expression, function(f) fread(f, select = c("gene_id", "TPM"))))
expr <- expr[grepl("^ENSG", gene_id) & !grepl("_PAR_Y$", gene_id),
             .(tpm = mean(TPM), n_rep = .N), by = .(gene_key = sub("\\..*$", "", gene_id))]
stopifnot(all(expr$n_rep == length(cfg$expression)))

summary <- fread(file.path(tables, "cluster_summary.tsv"))
m <- fread(file.path(tables, "molecule_assignments.tsv.gz"))
tss <- unique(m[, .(cluster, tss_id, gene_id, gene_name, pi)])
tss[, tpm := expr$tpm[match(sub("\\..*$", "", gene_id), expr$gene_key)]]
tss[, cluster := factor(cluster, levels = pol2_numeric_clusters(summary$cluster))]
message(sum(is.na(tss$tpm)), " of ", nrow(tss), " cluster/TSS pairs have no TPM")

d <- tss[is.finite(tpm)]
out <- d[, {
  ok <- is.finite(pi) & is.finite(tpm)
  correlation <- if(sum(ok)>=3L) suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(pi[ok],tpm[ok],method="spearman")) else NULL
  list(n_tss=.N,median_tpm=median(tpm),frac_tpm_ge1=mean(tpm>=1),median_pi=median(pi,na.rm=TRUE),
    rho_pi_tpm=if(is.null(correlation)) NA_real_ else unname(correlation$estimate),
    p_rho=if(is.null(correlation)) NA_real_ else correlation$p.value,n_pi_tpm=sum(ok))
},by=cluster]
# TPM of each cluster's TSSs against all other clusters' TSSs.
out[, p_tpm_vs_rest := vapply(as.character(cluster), function(cl)
  stats::wilcox.test(d[cluster == cl, tpm], d[cluster != cl, tpm])$p.value, numeric(1))]
out[, `:=`(fdr_rho = adjust_bh(p_rho), fdr_tpm_vs_rest = adjust_bh(p_tpm_vs_rest))]
setorder(out, cluster)
kw <- stats::kruskal.test(tpm ~ cluster, data = d)
print(out)

colors <- cluster_id_palette(levels(d$cluster))
boxes <- ggplot(d, aes(cluster, log10(tpm + 1), fill = cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Cluster (numeric order)", y = "log10(TPM + 1)", title = "Expression of each cluster's TSSs",
       subtitle = sprintf("ENCSR820PHH, mean of 2 replicates; Kruskal-Wallis p = %.2g", kw$p.value)) +
  theme_fiberseq("classic", base_size = 10)
labels <- out[, .(cluster, label = sprintf("rho = %.2f\nn = %d", rho_pi_tpm, n_pi_tpm))]
scatter <- ggplot(d[is.finite(pi) & pi > 0], aes(log10(pi), log10(tpm + 1), colour = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) + facet_wrap(~cluster, nrow = 1) +
  geom_text(data = labels, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "log10(pausing index)", y = "log10(TPM + 1)", title = "Pausing index vs expression within each cluster (Spearman)") +
  theme_fiberseq("bw", base_size = 10)
combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(boxes, scatter, ncol=1,rel_heights=c(1,.9))
save_figure(combined,file.path(cfg$output,"plots","pi_expression_by_cluster.pdf"),width=14,height=8)
list(plot=combined,summary=out)
})
```


## Histone marks at the TSS

Bulk GM12878 histone ChIP-seq fold change over control (`histone_marks` in config:
ENCODE4 GRCh38 reprocessing of the Broad ENCODE2 experiments, pooled replicates) around
each clustered molecule's FANTOM5 TSS, strand-oriented. Each 50-bp bin is the
coverage-weighted mean signal. A cluster's curve is the mean over its molecules, so a
TSS weighs in proportion to its molecules. Each panel shows one histone mark, with
all cluster curves overlaid in numeric order and no all-molecule reference. The ChIP is GM12878 locus-level evidence, not a measurement on each molecule
or donor, and molecules at the same TSS share its signal. Descriptive only.

```{r histone-analysis, include=FALSE}
histone_result <- local({
  profile_path <- file.path(cfg$output,"tables","histone_cluster_profiles.tsv.gz")
  if (!file.exists(profile_path)) stop("Run --stage histone-inputs before knitting")
  profiles <- fread(profile_path)
  plot <- pol2_plot_histone_profiles(profiles, clusters)
  save_figure(plot, file.path(cfg$output, "plots", "histone_profiles_by_cluster.pdf"), width = 16, height = 4.5)
  stacked <- pol2_plot_histone_profiles(profiles, clusters, stacked = TRUE)
  save_figure(stacked, file.path(cfg$output, "plots", "histone_profiles_by_cluster_stacked.pdf"), width = 16, height = 12)
  list(overlay = plot, stacked = stacked)
})
```

```{r histone-figure, fig.width=16, fig.height=4.5}
print(histone_result$overlay)
```


The second view stacks clusters 1–7 vertically, with one histone mark per column.
Each mark uses the same y-axis range across clusters; the all-molecule reference
is omitted.

```{r histone-stacked-figure, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
print(histone_result$stacked)
```
